claims.claim: Public Service Enterprise Group identity and NYSE tradability are validated; current underwriting uses SEC/issuer primary evidence plus a separate market-data surface, with duplicate issuer origin collapsed.

unknowns.unknown: Final financing mix, future rate-case outcomes and nuclear contract pricing remain unresolved and reduce confidence.

claims.claim: PSEG couples regulated grid modernization with firm nuclear generation, creating durable electricity-demand exposure bounded by regulatory recovery and financing discipline.

thesisQuality.basis: Regulated grid investment plus owned nuclear generation addresses durable reliability/load-growth needs, but realized value remains rate-recovery and financing dependent.

financialOperatingMomentum.basis: Six-month non-GAAP operating earnings rose to $1.203B from $1.102B and operating cash flow improved; large capex and financing costs temper the band.

marketValuationOpportunity.basis: At $66.56 on Sep.24 versus 2026 operating EPS guidance and long-term 6%-8% earnings-growth target, valuation appears balanced-to-moderately attractive rather than exceptional.

catalystScore.basis: Rate-base investment, load growth and prospective nuclear contracting are identifiable catalysts, but contract timing/economics remain unresolved.

governancePower.basis: Management has maintained explicit capital/rate-base/earnings targets and operational restoration evidence; current sources do not justify an exceptional stewardship score.

alignment2036.basis: Transmission/distribution modernization and 3,758 MW carbon-free baseload nuclear capacity directly serve durable electricity reliability and load-growth needs.

crossDivisionLeverage.basis: Regulated electric/gas infrastructure and nuclear generation provide multiple related demand engines, though geographic/regulatory concentration remains material.

bottleneckControl.basis: Owned regulated grid infrastructure and firm nuclear generation participate in real capacity/reliability constraints with long capital lead times.

scenarioRobustness.basis: Regulated network investment and firm generation remain useful across several demand/decarbonization scenarios, offset by New Jersey regulatory concentration.

substitutionResilience.basis: Utility networks and baseload nuclear assets are difficult to replace quickly, but alternative generation/storage and policy choices constrain the score.

supplyChainResilience.basis: Operational restoration performance supports resilience, but current evidence does not establish exceptional supplier/fuel redundancy.

pricingPower.basis: Regulated cost recovery and nuclear market exposure support some value capture, but affordability/rate-case outcomes constrain unilateral pricing power.

riskEvidence.basis: Large $24B-$28B capital program creates financing, depreciation, regulatory-recovery and execution exposure; nuclear contracting economics remain uncertain.

dataConfidenceEvidence.basis: Current SEC filing, issuer results and current market quote cover operating trajectory and valuation; independent operating corroboration and final financing/contract economics remain limited.

scoreRecord.thesis: PSEG couples regulated grid modernization with scarce firm nuclear generation, giving it durable exposure to rising electricity demand and reliability needs, with value realization bounded by regulatory recovery and financing discipline.
scoreRecord.keyRisk: Capital intensity, financing costs, regulatory affordability and uncertain nuclear-contract economics can dilute rate-base and generation value.
scoreRecord.nextCatalyst: Progress on incremental regulated investment approvals and/or multi-year nuclear output contracting.

risks.risk: Capital intensity, financing costs and regulatory recovery remain material.
